# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yu_2025_paliperidone_human"))$reference`
* Description (dog): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yu_2025_paliperidone_dog"))$description`
* Description (human): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yu_2025_paliperidone_human"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2025.1507828>

Yu 2025 built a semi-mechanistic "muscle compartment" model for
intramuscular nanocrystal suspensions of paliperidone palmitate. The
injected solid is split by mass into twelve particle-size bins (the
0-2, 2-5, 5-10, 10-20, ..., 90-100 percent mass percentiles of the
particle-size distribution). After a bin-specific lag time each bin
dissolves into the injection-site fluid by the diffusion-layer model
(Equation 1):

$$
\frac{dSolid_n}{dt} = -N_n \frac{D}{h} 4\pi r_n (r_n + h)
  \left(S - \frac{RegionalDissolved}{V_{region}}\right),
\qquad t > t_{lag,n}
$$

with $r_n$ the radius of a particle of bin $n$, which shrinks as the bin
dissolves while the particle count $N_n$ stays fixed. Dissolved drug is
carried away by local blood flow (Equation 2) into a one-compartment
central disposition model (Equation 3).

The model was first developed in beagle dogs for the Invega Sustenna
reference suspension (R) and two Livzon test suspensions (T1, T2), with
the bin lag times and bioavailability derived from the dog plasma
profiles. It was then extrapolated to humans by replacing the disposition
with Samtani 2009 values and scaling the diffusion coefficient and the
injection-site clearance by the human-to-dog muscle blood-flow ratio
(73/350). The package ships both:

* `Yu_2025_paliperidone_dog` -- the beagle-dog model;
* `Yu_2025_paliperidone_human` -- the human extrapolation.

Both select the product with two indicators, `FORM_PALIPERIDONE_T1` and
`FORM_PALIPERIDONE_T2` (both 0 = reference R). One dose record into
`depot` (mg) is all that is needed; the model splits it across the bins.

# Population

Dogs (Section 2.5.1): male beagle dogs, 7-9 months old, 9-11 kg, each
given one intramuscular buttock injection of 50 mg paliperidone palmitate
as R, T1 or T2, with plasma sampled to 36 days. The number of dogs per
product is not reported.

Humans (Sections 2.6.2 and 3.3): no human data were fitted. The authors
simulated 300 virtual individuals after a single 50 mg injection and
compared product R against the mean profile reported by Samtani 2009.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Yu_2025_paliperidone_dog")()$population` and
`readModelDb("Yu_2025_paliperidone_human")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Dog value | Human value | Source location |
|----------------------|-----------|-------------|-----------------|
| Equation 1: `d/dt(depot)`, `d/dt(diss_bin<n>)` | n/a | n/a | Equation 1 |
| Equation 2: `d/dt(injsite)` | n/a | n/a | Equation 2 |
| Equation 3: `d/dt(central)` | n/a | n/a | Equation 3 |
| `lkel` (1/h) | log(ln 2 / 7.6) = log(0.0912) | log(0.0127) | Dog: Section 3.1.2 / Table 1 half-life 7.6 h; human: Table 4 |
| `lvc` (L) | log(8.5) | log(391) | Table 1 / Table 6; Table 4 |
| `lcltrans` (mL/h) | log(35) | log(7.3) | Table 1 CLdist; Table 4 CLtrans (see deviations: printed as L/h) |
| `lvregion` (mL) | log(0.5) | log(0.5) | Section 3.1.1 |
| `ldcoef` (m^2/s) | log(4.69e-12) | log(9.78e-13) | Section 3.3; Table 4 |
| `lhdl` (um) | log(3) | log(3) | Table 1 |
| `rho` (g/cm^3) | 1.2 | 1.2 | Table 1 |
| `sol` (mg/mL) | 0.00704 | 0.00704 | Table 1 |
| `lfdepot`, `lfdepot_t1`, `lfdepot_t2` | log(1), log(0.83), log(0.72) | same | Table 6 |
| `frac_bin1` ... `frac_bin12` | 0.02, 0.03, 0.05, 0.10 x 9 | same | Section 2.6.1 |
| `rad_bin<n>`, `rad_t1_bin<n>`, `rad_t2_bin<n>` (um) | Table 7 rows R, T1, T2 | same | Table 7 |
| `tlag_bin<n>`, `tlag_t1_bin<n>`, `tlag_t2_bin<n>` (h) | Table 2 rows R, T1, T2 | same | Table 2 |

# Simulation

The model is deterministic (the paper reports no between-subject
variability or residual error), so one subject per product reproduces the
typical profiles.

```{r simulate}
mod_dog <- readModelDb("Yu_2025_paliperidone_dog")
mod_hum <- readModelDb("Yu_2025_paliperidone_human")

products <- tibble::tibble(
  id = 1:3,
  product = c("R", "T1", "T2"),
  FORM_PALIPERIDONE_T1 = c(0L, 1L, 0L),
  FORM_PALIPERIDONE_T2 = c(0L, 0L, 1L)
)

make_events <- function(obs_times) {
  dose <- products |>
    mutate(time = 0, amt = 50, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(products, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    as.data.frame()
}

# Dog: 36 days (last sampling day); human: 126 days (last Samtani 2009
# observation in Figure 5).
ev_dog <- make_events(seq(0, 36 * 24, by = 1))
ev_hum <- make_events(seq(0, 126 * 24, by = 2))

sim_dog <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_dog, events = ev_dog, keep = "product") |>
  as.data.frame()
sim_hum <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_hum, events = ev_hum, keep = "product") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

# Replicate published figures

## Dog model (Figures 4 and 6)

Figure 4 of the paper is labelled as the reference sample, but its
plasma panel is identical to Figure 6A (T1), and its solid-mass panel
starts each 10 percent bin at about 4.15 mg (= 0.83 x 50 mg x 0.10, the T1
bioavailability) with bins 11 and 12 starting to dissolve at day 6 (the
T1 lag time of 144 h). It is therefore reproduced here with T1.

```{r figure-4a-6}
# Replicates Figure 4A / 6A (T1) and Figure 6B (T2) of Yu 2025, plus R.
ggplot(sim_dog, aes(time / 24, Cc, colour = product)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "Paliperidone plasma concentration (ng/mL)",
    colour = "Product",
    title = "Dog plasma paliperidone after 50 mg IM",
    caption = "Replicates Figures 4A and 6 of Yu 2025."
  )
```

```{r figure-4b}
# Replicates Figure 4B of Yu 2025: dissolved paliperidone at the injection site.
sim_dog |>
  filter(product == "T1") |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, Cinj)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "Dissolved paliperidone at injection site (ng/mL)",
    title = "Dog, product T1: local dissolved concentration",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4B of Yu 2025."
  )
```

```{r figure-4c}
# Replicates Figure 4C of Yu 2025: undissolved solid mass in each bin. The
# solid left in bin n is its starting mass (frac_bin<n> x F x dose) minus
# what it has released.
frac <- c(0.02, 0.03, 0.05, rep(0.10, 9))
solid_t1 <- sim_dog |>
  filter(product == "T1") |>
  select(time, starts_with("diss_bin")) |>
  pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "bin", values_to = "dissolved") |>
  mutate(
    n = as.integer(sub("diss_bin", "", bin)),
    solid = frac[n] * 0.83 * 50 - dissolved,
    bin = factor(paste("Bin", n), levels = paste("Bin", 1:12))
  )
ggplot(solid_t1, aes(time / 24, solid, colour = bin)) +
  geom_line() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 30)) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "Undissolved mass (mg)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Dog, product T1: solid mass per bin",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4C of Yu 2025."
  )
```

## Human model (Figures 5 and 7)

```{r figure-5-7}
# Replicates the median curves of Figure 5 (R) and Figure 7 (T1, T2).
ggplot(sim_hum, aes(time / 24, Cc, colour = product)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "Paliperidone plasma concentration (ng/mL)",
    colour = "Product",
    title = "Human plasma paliperidone after 50 mg IM (typical value)",
    caption = "Replicates the 50th-percentile curves of Figures 5 and 7 of Yu 2025."
  )
```

# PKNCA validation

AUC0-t is computed over the paper's windows: 0-36 days for the dogs
(Table 3) and 0-126 days for humans (Table 5, the last Samtani 2009
observation).

```{r pknca}
run_nca <- function(sim, events, tend) {
  conc <- sim |>
    filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
    select(id, time, Cc, product)
  conc <- bind_rows(
    conc,
    conc |> distinct(id, product) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
  ) |>
    distinct(id, product, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    arrange(id, product, time)
  dose <- events |>
    filter(evid == 1) |>
    select(id, time, amt, product)
  intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = tend, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | product + id),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ time | product + id),
    intervals = intervals
  ))
}
nca_dog <- run_nca(sim_dog, ev_dog, 36 * 24)
nca_hum <- run_nca(sim_hum, ev_hum, 126 * 24)
```

## Comparison against published values

The reference values are the paper's own **simulated** AUC0-t and Cmax
(Tables 3 and 5), which is what a correct implementation should
reproduce. The observed values are listed in the text below.

```{r nca-compare-dog}
published_dog <- tibble::tribble(
  ~product, ~auclast, ~cmax,
  "R",      64962,    262.7,
  "T1",     53963,    225.8,
  "T2",     46808,    209.9
)
cmp_dog <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_dog,
  reference = published_dog,
  by = "product",
  units = c(auclast = "ng*h/mL", cmax = "ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_dog, caption = "Dog: simulated vs. Yu 2025 Table 3 simulated values. * differs by >20%.")
```

```{r nca-compare-human}
published_hum <- tibble::tribble(
  ~product, ~auclast, ~cmax,
  "R",      10009,    8.605,
  "T1",     8324,     8.234,
  "T2",     7220,     7.877
)
cmp_hum <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_hum,
  reference = published_hum,
  by = "product",
  units = c(auclast = "ng*h/mL", cmax = "ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_hum, caption = "Human: simulated vs. Yu 2025 Table 5 simulated values. * differs by >20%.")
```

Observed values for comparison: in dogs, AUC0-t 59,753 / 53,546 / 44,581
ng*h/mL and Cmax 286.0 / 221.0 / 194.0 ng/mL for R / T1 / T2 (Table 3); in
humans, Samtani 2009 reports AUC0-t 10,062 ng*h/mL and Cmax 9.257 ng/mL
for product R (Table 5).

```{r nca-assert}
nca_tab <- function(res) {
  as.data.frame(res) |>
    filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cmax")) |>
    select(product, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
}
chk_dog <- nca_tab(nca_dog) |> left_join(published_dog, by = "product", suffix = c("_sim", "_pub"))
chk_hum <- nca_tab(nca_hum) |> left_join(published_hum, by = "product", suffix = c("_sim", "_pub"))
chk <- bind_rows(chk_dog, chk_hum)
# Deterministic model, no random draws, so these hold on any machine.
# AUC0-t is fixed by F x dose / CL and lands within 1%; the per-bin
# dissolution shapes the peak, where the realised differences are
# 0.5-5% (dog) and 3-7% (human).
stopifnot(
  all(abs(chk$auclast_sim / chk$auclast_pub - 1) < 0.02),
  all(abs(chk$cmax_sim / chk$cmax_pub - 1) < 0.10)
)
```

## Mass balance

Everything injected (F x dose) is eventually absorbed and eliminated, so
the area under the curve to infinity equals F x dose / CL. The 126-day
human window holds essentially all of it.

```{r mass-balance}
kel_h <- 0.0127
vc_h <- 391
auc_expected <- c(R = 1, T1 = 0.83, T2 = 0.72) * 50 / (kel_h * vc_h) * 1000
auc_sim <- nca_tab(nca_hum)
auc_sim$expected <- auc_expected[auc_sim$product]
knitr::kable(auc_sim |> select(product, auclast, expected),
  caption = "Human AUC0-126 day vs. F x dose / CL (ng*h/mL)", digits = 0
)
stopifnot(all(abs(auc_sim$auclast / auc_sim$expected - 1) < 0.01))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

The paper's printed values contain several inconsistencies. Each was
resolved by the paper's own simulated outputs (Tables 3 and 5, Figure 4),
not by fitting:

- **Dog elimination rate constant.** Table 1 prints `Ke,dog = 0.0693 /h`
  but states it was calculated from the 7.6 h half-life, which gives
  ln 2 / 7.6 = 0.0912 /h (0.0693 /h is ln 2 / 10 h). With F x dose / (ke x
  Vd) the half-life value reproduces the simulated AUC0-t of Table 3 for
  all three products to within 1%, while 0.0693 /h overpredicts it by
  about 30%. The model uses ln 2 / 7.6.
- **Dog diffusion coefficient.** Table 1 and Section 3.1.1 give a fitted
  dog value of 1.17e-11 m^2/s, but the human derivation in Section 3.3
  scales a dog value of 4.69e-12 m^2/s ((73/350) x 4.69e-12 = 9.78e-13,
  the Table 4 human value). The 4.69e-12 value reproduces the Table 3
  Cmax values and Figure 4B/4C; 1.17e-11 overpredicts Cmax by 10-23%. The
  dog model uses 4.69e-12 m^2/s.
- **Injection-site clearance units.** Table 1 gives `CLdist = 35 L/h` and
  Table 4 `CLtrans = 7.3 L/h`. With the 0.5 mL injection-site volume, a
  clearance of 35 L/h would keep the local dissolved concentration near
  30 ng/mL and give a dog Cmax 1.8-3.5 times that of Table 3. Figure 4B shows
  local dissolved concentrations near 5000 ng/mL, which requires 35 mL/h.
  Both values are therefore used in mL/h.
- **Particle size as radius.** Table 7 reports a "particle size" per bin.
  Used as the particle radius in Equation 1, the bin sizes reproduce
  Table 3 Cmax to within 5% and the bin dissolution times of Figure 4C
  (bins 11 and 12 of T1 start at day 6 and are gone by about day 15 and
  20). Used as a diameter they make every bin dissolve about twice as
  fast and overpredict dog Cmax by 11-24%. The model uses them as radii.
- **Equation 1 particle count.** As printed, the cube root in Equation 1
  is `(3 Solid_n / (4 pi rho))^(1/3)`, the radius of one sphere holding the
  whole bin mass; multiplied by `N_n` this gives near-instantaneous
  dissolution. The model uses the standard diffusion-layer form, in which
  the radius is that of one particle, `(3 Solid_n / (4 pi rho N_n))^(1/3)`,
  with `N_n` fixed by the starting bin mass and particle size.
- **Figure 4 product.** Figure 4 is captioned with the reference sample,
  but its panels match product T1 (see above).
- **Human parameters carried over from the dog.** Diffusion-layer
  thickness, solid density, solubility, injection-site volume, the bin lag
  times and the bioavailabilities have no human values in the paper; the
  model carries the dog values over, as the paper describes. The human T1
  and T2 AUC0-t of Table 5 are 0.83 and 0.72 times that of R, which
  confirms the carried-over bioavailabilities.
- **Variability not reported.** The paper simulated 300 virtual humans
  and shows 5th-95th percentile bands (Figures 5 and 7), but does not
  report which parameters varied or by how much. Both models are
  typical-value models with no random effects or residual error. The
  paper's median curves have a slower terminal decline (for example 0.6
  and 0.4 ng/mL at day 75 for T1 and T2, versus about 0.3 and 0.2 ng/mL
  here), as expected when variable absorption is summarised by a median;
  Table 5 Cmax is reproduced to within 3-7%.
- **Dose.** The 50 mg dose is treated as 50 mg of paliperidone, as in the
  paper: the human AUC of Table 5 equals 50 mg / CL with the Samtani 2009
  clearance. Hydrolysis of the palmitate ester is not modelled.
- **Repeated injections.** The model was published for a single
  injection. A second dose into `depot` is pooled with what remains of the
  first, and the bin lag times restart from the latest injection, so
  multiple-dose simulations are an extrapolation of the published model.
